summary: Iteration 6 — Premium membership + Stripe payments + free-tier gating/metering. 37/37 pytest cases passed in 147.5s against the preview URL. (1) GET /api/membership/plans returns premium=false + exactly the two configured plans (monthly $9.99/30d, annual $79.99/365d, currency=usd, labels present); requires auth (401 without token). (2) FREE gating: with premium_until unset AND usage cleared, all 6 premium-only endpoints correctly return HTTP 402 with a Premium-copy detail — POST /packing/plan, /capsule/build, /shop-check, /insights/missing-piece, /insights/health-report, /items/{id}/compatibility — plus POST /profiles (attempting a 2nd household profile) returns 402. enforce_limit is invoked BEFORE any AI/DB heavy work so all 402s return in <100ms. (3) FREE metering: POST /stylist/suggest returns 200 five times then 402 on the 6th within the same day; POST /beauty/suggest against David (no skin_tone/undertone) returns 400 with a helpful 'Add your skin tone…' detail and — critically — does NOT increment the monthly beauty counter (verified in db.usage). First call from Aura (skin_tone=medium, undertone=warm) returns 200 with the expected keys (summary/palette/makeup/hair); the immediate 2nd call in the same month returns 402. (4) PAYMENTS: POST /payments/checkout {plan:'monthly'} → 200 with a real https://checkout.stripe.com URL + session_id, and a payment_transactions row is inserted with the correct amount (9.99), plan, account_id and payment_status='initiated', processed=false; annual plan symmetrically inserts amount 79.99. Invalid plan → 400; unauthenticated → 401. GET /payments/status/{session_id} for a real (unpaid) session returns 200 with payment_status != 'paid' AND does NOT grant premium (users.premium_until remained unset, response.premium=false). Unknown session id → 404. (5) PREMIUM (grant via db.users.updateOne premium_until=2099…): the same six previously-402 endpoints all return 200 with valid AI JSON (packing.capsule_item_ids, capsule.summary+capsule_item_ids, shop-check.verdict ∈ {Buy,Skip,Maybe}, missing-piece, health-report, compatibility.versatility_score+matches). Stylist called 6x in a row on premium — all 200 (bypasses the 5/day cap); beauty called 2x in the same month — both 200. GET /membership/plans reflects premium=true. (6) Household cap on premium: created 4 additional profiles to reach 6 total, then the 7th attempt returned 400 ('A household can have up to 6 members.'); the 4 test profiles were cascaded and deleted at teardown. (7) Regression: items list carries integer pairs_count, full items CRUD roundtrip (create → get → update → delete → 404), /insights, /laundry, outfits CRUD, plans CRUD, /wear log, /analyze-item free (with & without category_hint — hint honoured) all continued to return 200. Cleanup verified: premium_until unset, 0 usage docs, only the 2 seeded profiles remain, 0 non-Ready items, 0 leftover TEST_ items.

minor.issue: Still returns 200 (not 201) on creation — carried over from earlier iterations.
All resource-creation endpoints return 200 rather than 201 Created — cosmetic REST convention only, tests accept both.

Endpoint accepts ANY authenticated user's token to query a session id owned by another account — the session id is treated as the sole authorisation. Currently harmless because premium is granted to tx.account_id (not the caller), but session-id enumeration would leak payment_status of other accounts. Consider requiring tx.account_id == account.user_id.

action_items: None functionally required — membership, payments, gating, metering, premium unlock and household cap all behave to spec.
Optional (security): scope /api/payments/status/{session_id} to only the tx.account_id owner (return 404 for other callers) to prevent cross-account payment-status enumeration.
critical_code_review_comments: enforce_limit (server.py:183-203) correctly checks scope.premium FIRST, so premium accounts bypass all metering and Premium-only gating in a single line. The FREE_LIMITS dict is the single source of truth — every non-listed feature falls through to the 402 branch (line 190-191). Clean design.

beauty_suggest (server.py:1372-1405) puts the skin-tone 400 BEFORE enforce_limit — this is the exact ordering the PRD requires so a missing-profile 400 does not consume the 1/month credit. Verified in tests.

_grant_premium (server.py:325-342) is idempotent and correctly EXTENDS an existing premium_until instead of overwriting it (base = max(now, current)). Good for stacked purchases. Only called from the 'paid' + 'not processed' branch of /payments/status, which then flips processed=true so double-grants are impossible.

create_checkout (server.py:288-322) records payment_transactions with account_id at creation time — this is what /payments/status uses to grant entitlement. Combined with metadata={account_id,plan,kind:'premium'} on the Stripe session, this is well-tied.

create_profile (server.py:407-426) enforces (a) 402 on 2nd profile for free, (b) 400 on 7th for premium — both branches exercised and correct. The initial ensure_default_profile call means count is always ≥1 by the time the cap check runs, which matches PRD's 'exactly 1 wardrobe profile' rule for Free.

server.py is 1468 lines — approaching the 700-line split threshold from the review guidelines. Consider extracting membership/payments and each AI feature module into separate routers when it hits 2k. Not blocking.
STRIPE_API_KEY is read from env and the checkout endpoint returns 500 if unset — good fail-fast. Live testing confirmed the emergent test-proxy key produces real checkout.stripe.com URLs.

rca_of_issue: No bugs found. Membership/payments/gating/metering are implemented correctly and end-to-end: (a) is_premium is derived purely from users.premium_until (whole household), (b) enforce_limit is a single choke-point checking premium then the FREE_LIMITS dict for metered features and 402'ing everything else, (c) beauty_suggest orders the skin-tone 400 BEFORE enforce_limit so a UX-nudging error never eats the monthly credit (verified against db.usage), (d) create_checkout+payment_status split entitlement grant from session creation and use tx.processed as an idempotency flag, so entitlement can only be granted on the transition 'unpaid→paid' exactly once.
